collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and a teen aged 14-17)

collection.description: An elder envies the young until a teen runs up upset: remember the hard parts of being young, or envy them anyway.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is watching (friend) and (friend.his/her) friends run and shout and leap into the sea from the rocks. For a moment, (subject) envies them terribly: the energy, the bendy knees, the whole long life ahead. Then (friend) comes running up, red-faced, almost in tears about something one of the others said.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) listens to the whole story, which is very complicated and involves who sat next to whom. (friend) is miserable about it. And (subject) remembers, suddenly and vividly, what it was like to be sixteen: how big everything felt, how much everything mattered, how nobody understood. "I wouldn't go back for anything," (subject.he/she) says, kindly. (friend) is outraged. "That's not HELPFUL." (subject) laughs. (subject.He/she) helps anyway.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) comforts (friend), and (friend) runs back to the rocks, already over it, and leaps into the sea with a shriek. (subject) watches. Yes, being young was hard. But (subject.he/she) still misses those knees. (subject.He/she) goes home and tries jumping off a small rock into the stream. It's undignified. It's also wonderful. (subject.He/she) doesn't tell anyone.
